lesson.title: Pass it on: mesh networks
lesson.subtitle: How messages hop to the gateway, and get through when a sensor fails

video.title: Pass it on: mesh networks
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor at the edge of the school farm, pointing at a small sensor on a stake far across the field; the office roof is a dot in the distance.
scenes.animation: A radio ring spreads from the sensor and fades out long before the office.
scenes.narration: Our far-field sensor could never reach the school office. Its radio reaches two hundred metres; the office is six hundred away. So we didn't buy a bigger radio. We asked its neighbours to pass the message on.

scenes.visual: Darsi title card with the IoT track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: mesh networks, where devices pass messages along to get them home.

scenes.visual: A hub in the centre with lines to five devices around it like a star; a sixth device sits outside the circle of range, with no line.
scenes.animation: Lines draw from the hub; the far device blinks grey.
scenes.narration: Most networks you know are a star: every device talks straight to one hub, like a router. That's simple, but every device must be in range of the hub. Anything farther away is cut off.

scenes.visual: Sensors dotted across a field; a message dot jumps from the far sensor to a neighbour, then another, then the gateway at the office.
scenes.animation: The dot hops sensor to sensor; each hop leaves a short glowing line.
scenes.narration: In a mesh network, devices pass messages for each other. A sensor sends its reading to a neighbour in range, who passes it on. Each step is called a hop. Hop by hop, the message reaches the gateway.

scenes.visual: A dusty school pitch: the ball zigzags between players towards the goal; one player is blocked, and the ball swings round him.
scenes.animation: Passes draw as dashed arrows; a blocked arrow turns grey and a new one curves round.
scenes.narration: It's like football. Nobody kicks the ball from one end straight into the goal. The team passes it, player to player. And if one player is marked, the ball goes another way.

scenes.visual: Amina beside a field map; a goat nudges a sensor stake over. Two answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A goat knocks over a sensor in the middle of the field. What happens to messages from the sensors behind it?

scenes.visual: The fallen sensor turns grey; messages from behind it curve round through two other sensors and still reach the gateway.
scenes.animation: The old route fades; a new route lights up hop by hop.
scenes.narration: They take another route, through neighbours that still work. It may cost an extra hop, but they get through. That's why a mesh keeps working when one device fails.

scenes.visual: The field map again: one sensor linked by a single line; a wide empty strip between two groups; the gateway with a red outline.
scenes.animation: Each weak point pulses red as it is named.
scenes.narration: But a mesh still has weak points. A sensor with only one neighbour hangs by a thread. A gap wider than the radio's range splits the network in two. And if the gateway fails, nothing gets out at all.

scenes.visual: A small relay box on a pole drops into the empty strip; new lines join the two groups. A second line reaches the lonely sensor. A solar panel appears on the gateway.
scenes.animation: Relay drops in; links draw across the gap.
scenes.narration: The fix is often cheap: a relay, a simple radio that only passes messages on. Put one in a gap, and the two halves join. Give lonely sensors a second neighbour. And keep the gateway powered.

scenes.visual: Battery gauges above each sensor; the ones nearest the gateway drain fastest as many message dots pass through them.
scenes.animation: Dots stream through the inner sensors; their gauges drop.
scenes.narration: But every hop costs battery on the sensor that relays it, and adds a little delay. So sensors next to the gateway work hardest: they carry everyone's messages.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor by a riverbank map: one sensor near the water, a single line to a neighbour on low ground. Two answer cards bounce in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Zainab's sensor by the river has only one neighbour, and floods keep knocking that neighbour over. What's the best fix?

scenes.visual: Four icons line up: a hop arrow, a detour, a relay, the gateway.
scenes.animation: Icons line up left to right, 250 ms apart.
scenes.narration: Add a relay on higher ground: a second neighbour means a second route. Remember: messages hop from neighbour to neighbour to the gateway. When one device fails, they find another way. Fill gaps with relays, and look after the gateway.

scenes.visual: A student's desk: a hand-drawn farm map with dots, a piece of string held from one dot to another, pencil lines between dots.
scenes.animation: The string swings from dot to dot; lines draw where it reaches.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: a paper mesh. Draw ten sensors and a gateway on a map. Cut a string as long as the radio's range, and link every two sensors it reaches. Find one that's cut off, and add a relay to rescue it.

checkpoints.prompt: A goat knocks over a sensor in the middle of a mesh. What happens to messages from the sensors behind it?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — their neighbours pass them along another route to the gateway, maybe with an extra hop.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — most sensors in a mesh hear more than one neighbour, so messages go round the broken one.

checkpoints.prompt: Zainab's river sensor has only one neighbour, and floods keep knocking it over. What's the best fix?

options.text: Add a relay on higher ground

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a relay out of the flood's reach gives it a second route, so one fallen neighbour can't cut it off.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — its battery isn't the problem: its single link is. A relay on higher ground gives it a second route.
